extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and artisan-operators (17th-century readers of Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Composing and reporting observational and experimental accounts of natural phenomena, mineral assays, maritime/tidal observations, and practical craft methods as found in early-modern natural philosophy journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vitriol tract contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the nature, difference, choice, qualities and medical virtues of vitriol, together with the various ways of preparing both dry and liquid medicines out of that mineral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods used (e.g., the method of preparing vitriol used at Goslar); include nature, differences, selection/choice criteria, qualities, and medical uses; the author notes that if a process is 'now so generally known' an account may be unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tide observation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Record timings and heights of tides (annual spring tides in March and September, diurnal tides), relation to moon phase and bearing, and the influence of winds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric heights (feet/inches), timings (hours and quarter-hours), produce a tide-table (quarters of hours) showing flow and ebb durations (e.g., flowing 5 hours, ebbing 7 hours), note seasonal diurnal differences (evening vs morning), identify anomalies (e.g., 'boar' / head of flood at the Severn) and explain local geographic causes (straightening, shoaling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assaying minerals — exploratory tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sequential experimental tests to characterise a suspected metal/mineral: observe fumes in a reverberating fire; boil sample in water and observe residual alkali after evaporation; test with quicksilver and customary magistrals; try caput mortuum of vitriol and saltpetre; apply corrosive separating water with common salt to attempt dissolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed stepwise from non-destructive observation (colour of fumes) to chemical extractions; compare outcomes to known behaviours (e.g., whether mercury will amalgamate); when ordinary means fail, try regionally-known procedures (Peruvian boiling method), acids (aqua fortis) and tartareous salts; document each attempt and the observed products (yellow dirt, tinctures) rather than assuming identity with gold or silver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ore preparation for mercury amalgamation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce ore into small pieces; calcine in a reverberating oven with a moderate fire to free mineral and reveal corrosive mixtures by the colour of fumes; grind to a fine flour; sift and divide into several heaps to assay separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust additives according to the ore's 'peccant humour' (for sulphureous/antimonial ores add rust/dross of iron; for martial/iron-rich ores add sulphur and antimony powder); run small trial assays on each heap to estimate silver yield (common yields: 6, 12, 18 ounces per 100 pounds), then proportionally apply quicksilver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators for completion of mercury separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use visual and procedural signs to judge when mercury has separated silver: the 'colour of the mercury, coagulated by the silver in clear massy lumps' (pellas) is taken as a sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wash the mercury–ore mixture through three vessels in series to remove non-incorporated dust; observe pellas settling by weight to the bottom; remove amalgam, squeeze through coarse linen and beat to recover as much quicksilver as possible; form into moulded masses (Pineas de plata) and heat in a blind alembic so remaining mercury distils away, leaving silver to be melted with the 'liga' (royal toll considerations noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical field observation and reporting (miner travelogue)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting naturalistic or mining field observations, record context (location, guide presence), sensory effects (glittering canopy, dust corrosiveness), experiment sequence, hazards (sandfall, loss of light, corrosive dust), and immediate tests performed (scraping, rubbing, heating, boiling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include narrative of exploration (how you entered cave, guide behavior), precise experimental actions and their immediate outcomes (e.g., sample divided into spangles, fumes absent due to drying sand), and any health/hazard notes (corrosive acrimony endangering sight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subduing dangerous animals — practical technique reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Give clear, actionable techniques for handling dangerous fauna: e.g., to master and kill alligators: be armed with a long truncheon, attack sideways, strike on the shoulder and behind the fore-feet to lame them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain risks of incorrect approach (front-ways they are too nimble and may leap on the assailant); provide step-by-step physical actions and rationale (lame them to render unable to move).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical notes on pests and toxic plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Report immediate practical observations: tortoises die if their blood be heated; chegoes symptoms appear about a week after infection and removal requires extracting the whole bag; the Manchineel (Manchinel) apple is beautiful but fatally poisonous and its wood can blister skin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both descriptive danger warnings and practical handling guidance (extract entire brood bag to prevent remnants; avoid contact with green wood or falling drops from the tree).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting unusual biological phenomena (luminous insects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record anomalies and claimed applications: 'The shining flies...glowing and shining in the night, even when they are dead... applied... to a printed and written paper in the dark, and read it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note conditions of the observation (dead vs alive), claimed effects and any attempted demonstration; preserve skepticism but report practical implications and reproducibility notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for working convex spherical glasses on a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct an apparatus of a pole with a frame of concentric rings/ball to hold the lens-piece, a horizontal metal plane for grinding/polishing, and a levelling system of two planks with regulators to level the plate; grind with a turn-tool and sand, polish with paper cemented on the plane, and finish with gutters proportionable to the sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed setup instructions (how to fasten pole to ceiling or support, frame likened to a mariner's compass, regulators and wedges to level plate, use pendulum for levelling); advise that polishing on this instrument is long and tedious and recommend using traditional gutters for polishing after shaping; include diagrams and note expert opinion that the method may be difficult to scale for long focal lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory-reporting standards (respiration and rickets)
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting physiological theories, lay out mechanistic claims and physiological consequences: e.g., explain inspiration by elastic force and chest dilation, posit an aerial 'nitre' necessary to life that effects blood fermentation and muscle motion; for rickets, identify nutrition as involving nervous juice and blood and attribute unequal distribution (obstruction of spinal marrow) as cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine anatomical/physiological description with proposed causal hypotheses, note experimental or observational implications (plants needing nitrous air in soil; removal of obstructions and nervous strengthening as therapeutic aims), and suggest remedies consistent with the mechanism while acknowledging speculative status.
